title: The Pioneers
subtitle: Even if there is no path, even if there is no destination.

trails.title: Diagnosis Record - Awakened
trails.description: We absolutely respect the health rights of our employees.

content.text:
Diagnostic Subject: Lucy

    Examination Items: X-ray scanning, visualization, fluoroscopy, magnetic induction check, intelligence checks for age groups 6 to 60, including vision and hearing checks ...

    Clinical Manifestation: The subject's core briefly lost consciousness after channeling an incantation, then returned to normal. Considering the replaceability of the external shell, the damage is negligible. Only changes to the core are described below:

    Basically unchanged.

    The subject's core remains stable, with no apparent external injuries, nor any internal damage found. All examination indices are normal. It is speculated that the subject's external shell bore the brunt of the curse, and that the subject's spirit is greater than the material of the vessel—according to one of the current mainstream views, the consciousness of the awakened comes from some still unknown macro-arcanum phenomenon. Perhaps it is such arcane phenomena that override the side effects of the incantation, helping to overcome the curse directly affecting the core, so that the target does not die from the curse while the consciousness remains.

    Final Diagnosis: The subject's suggestion to further verify the side effects of the curse by using herself was agreed upon. However, according to past records, the awakened are not forever indestructible, so observation must be maintained, and the experiment must be terminated immediately if symptoms such as core degradation or mental abnormalities occur.

items.text: The Pioneers
A deathly silence.
Until Enigma stumbles back, nearly falling over another person in the room.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: She's dead?
The piston lies motionless on the ground, as lifeless as any other object.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: This is what you wanted to show me?
His heart pounds in his ears as he pants, fists clenched and slick with sweat.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: To watch her utter a curse that's always brought death, only to die in vain?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: And you just let it happen?!
Ulrich looks at him, his voice poised and steady.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Calm down.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Calm down? She's dead, right there! You murderer!

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: We have already repeated this experiment many times.
Enigma is in disbelief.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: "Many times"? What?! You've sent people to their deaths over and over again?
The ferrofluid flows again, forming a shape that Enigma can only interpret as disdain.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Look at you, Adler, peeing your pants over a "curse." The human boy is so scared that he forgot to ask the crucial question—

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Did the ritual work?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: What, what do you mean? The curse, the side effect killed her. The experiment failed. Is that not what happened?

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: No, triggering the curse and failure are two separate things. I was the first one to recite the incantation. Way before Dora.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: When I read it aloud, it worked. I felt the warmth of a miraculous blessing on my head, soft, light as a feather.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: I told Madam Lucy right away, but as soon as she left the room, the "curse" hit me, and I began to liquefy.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: There was no one else in the room. My liquid form had become too insubstantial to push the help button.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: A long darkness followed. After that, I woke up again in my original primitive form, the way I first came into this world.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Original primitive form?
The ferrofluid pulsates, which in Ulrich's body language is a nod.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Unlike humans, the Awakened have neither flesh nor nerves. We are pieces of consciousness, echoes of a primordial melody, that just happen to reside in material objects by chance.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: With a mind and a body combined, we could talk, learn, think like you do, and perform the experiment and endure the side effects.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: And this curse, for some reason, cannot affect the "primal consciousness" that caused our awakening in the first place.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: While human minds dissipate when their tangible bodies are destroyed, our minds reawaken regardless of the changes and destruction of our external bodies.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Of course, this was an assumption based on idealized circumstances, and I needed another Awakened being who could awaken in different bodies to confirm my theory. That is why I sought out Madam Lucy for cross-verification. The results ...

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Yes, it was an assumption! You said it yourself! You came back to life this time, but what about the next? Nothing is for sure in arcanum!

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: What if she never wakes up again? What if she dies for good?
He swats Enigma's hand away.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: We know what we are doing, human.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Stay out of this. Only the Awakened can carry out the experiment, so we must proceed.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: This has nothing to do with race. It is a sense of duty that every researcher should have possessed when they chose this path.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: We have to go beyond the limit. Not out of madness, but out of rationality.
Silence fills the room, like the beginning of time when there was no sound to be heard.
Then slowly, the piston starts to spin.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hm. We seem to have replicated Effect No. 2, and 117 of the Coleman lab's protective rituals were proven ineffective.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Write it down, Simone. This is the fourth time we have seen it. Also, No. 45 and 69 are related to it.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: We need to speed up. This is too slow.
The lights are back on again, and the piston is placed into a new body.
Being prepared for all possible outcomes requires a significant amount of metal material, but it is essential for data collection and analysis.
With a soft hum, the robot turns her head and looks at Enigma, surprised.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Adler, what are you doing here?

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I am glad to see you out of your room and working with us again.

items.speaker: Assistant Simone
items.text: No. He is not on the team, ma'am. He forced his way in here.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Oh? My apologies. I seem to lose a small amount of data when I reawaken.
She smiles at him, as she always does.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Still, I am glad that you are showing initiative, Adler. Were we supposed to talk?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: No. We have nothing more to discuss, ma'am. Ulrich has filled me in on everything.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: But I still worry whether the experiment's risks were properly assessed.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Assessments will only be assessments. Much is beyond measure when it comes to arcanum.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Perhaps "faith" plays a more important role here.
Enigma is caught off guard by her words.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'm surprised it is you talking about "faith," ma'am.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hm. It seems we both have the ability to surprise each other.
As they speak, the robot strolls over to her chair and sits back down.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You are right. "Assessments" could indeed be useful to us.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: It allows us to know the probabilities of success and failure based on established facts and past experience.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But when we find ourselves in uncharted darkness, with no information or past experience to guide us, how are assessments going to help us?
She ponders and stares into the void.
Perhaps the experiment did fry some circuits, she's more sentimental than usual.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: The only thing we have in such darkness is the unwavering faith to move forward.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: When the first steam engine whistled, I awoke into this world.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: At the beginning of this new life, my circuits were charged with a singular, primal desire: to progress.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: In the midst of that never-ending whistle, I have watched man build the towers of science and knowledge, and I have watched them unleash chaos and destruction.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: You, too, have been lost and deterred, but your engines of progress have never stopped churning. Always move forward, no matter the destination, you told yourselves.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Until the "Storm" brought everything to a standstill.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: But this is just a small setback. We are only back to the beginning, where we stumble blindly.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: And this time, I happen to have a cane.
She gives him a tender smile.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: No need to worry about me. I will not shut down as long as there is still hope for progress.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Hm. We have wasted a bit of time on data recovery.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: Come, Simone. Let us begin the next experiment.

items.speaker: Lucy
items.text: I hope to dissolve into paste this time, so we can easily handle it with a Coleman's ritual of transformation.
The human researcher knows that it'd be inappropriate for him to stay here any longer.
Gritting his teeth, he moves toward the door, trying his best to leave the horrific scene behind him.
Someone is waiting for him by the door.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Seen enough? We know what we are doing, and you are of no help here.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: It's been the same old story in this place for the past eight years.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: When your faith crumbled during the "Storm," it was us who took over the place and cleaned up after you.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: It was us who got things back up and running, put coals in the hearth, and blazed a trail when everyone was lost in the dark.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: I know you may not understand the intricacies of the arcanum, but please show some basic respect for our efforts.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Will you do the experiments yourself, Ulrich?

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Of course. I am not some emotional, unhelpful little punk.
Instead of his usual witty comeback, Enigma simply shakes his head in a slow motion.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Do you still remember Adams?
A sudden question that seems out of place.
The ferrofluid quivers. The name seems to unearth memories that have been buried for eight long years in the confines of this institution.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Adams, Roman, Adolph, Sylvia, Albert, Louise ... Those who were taken from us by the rain.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Melvin, Frances, Caroline, Leopold ... They volunteered for the field, but we never heard from them again.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Now we have Dora, Richard, Dawkins, and Victor on the list.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Life has a wicked sense of humor. My mentor, my classmates, my colleagues, each of them deserved to live more than me. But they're all gone now. There's only me talking to you, alive, useless.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Am I going to see your names on that list too, Ulrich?
In this rare moment, he lowers his head.
But soon, he raises his arms and slaps the man hard on the back.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Spare me the feelings, human.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Though I will take back my sarcastic jabs at you, it is not something a leader should do. Madam Lucy talked to me about the importance of teamwork.
He awkwardly pats the human on the shoulder, a clumsy attempt at friendliness.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Go back to your room, Adler. The arcanists will take over from here. Until we get the results, you won't be needed here.
Enigma heaves a breath.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I will say this, Ulrich. If you survive the experiments,
Alarmed by the opening words, Ulrich instinctively turns down his receiver to avoid hearing anything too warm.
That would be more painful than suffering through a hundred experimental side effects.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I'll submit the sincerest application to never be on the same team as you again.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: So neither of us will have to worry about teamwork. How's that sound?

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: Haha.
A curve that almost resembles a smile appears on his face.

items.speaker: Cryptography Lead
items.text: I will wait for that application, Adler.
Now. Roll up your sleeves and clear your mind.
This is not the time to grieve.
If human reasoning and arcane knowledge are not enough on their own ...
... perhaps a combination of the two can solve this problem?
The lab door is in shambles, its metal plate barely hanging on. A wooden sign reading "Keep Out" sways precariously, covered in bite marks and scratches.
Enigma takes a moment before finally knocking on the door.
A voice answers from within.
Who's there?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Adler Hofmann from the cryptography team. Is Medicine Pocket in?

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: I heard that they wrote a paper on the linear correlation between the purity of an arcanist's bloodline and their power. Can I get some more details on the research?
The door creaks open to reveal a youthful face. But she is not the genius he is looking for.
The lab technician looks at him through her glasses and hesitates a little.

items.speaker: Laboratory Technician
items.text: The paper is here. Help yourself. Sorry about the stains on it. I just took it out of the trash.

items.speaker: Laboratory Technician
items.text: If you're looking for Medicine Pocket, I'm afraid they just left.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: Left? To where?
There is a subtle conflict on her face. She is torn between covering for her colleague and following the rules.
It is more than enough for him to catch on.

items.speaker: Enigma
items.text: They left the building? Hasn't the countdown already begun?

items.speaker: Laboratory Technician
items.text: Erm, yes, and by regulations we are not to leave. But, uhm ...

items.speaker: Laboratory Technician
items.text: They said their new theory had to be verified in the "Storm."
TO BE CONTINUED…
